content: I just noticed that docs#instFiniteDimensionalRealComplex, which states that Complex is a finite dimensional real vector space, is in a file about the measure on the upper half plane. Surely this is not the right place? If so I'll PR a move.

So in the file the code is

-- backward-compatibility fixes
instance : MeasureSpace ℂ := inferInstance

instance : FiniteDimensional ℝ ℂ := inferInstance

Removing them does not break anything. @David Loeffler you're the author, what was the issue there?
These instances initially had backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency options applied. Since they're gone now, it should be fine to remove the duplicate instances as well. Do you want to pr?
Yup! What I don't understand is why they were added in the first place.

Etienne Marion said:

Yup! What I don't understand is why they were added in the first place.

These were only ever intended as temporary fixes: this code was first PR'd in the immediate aftermath of the Lean v4.29 isDefEq changes, which caused widespread general breakage in instances involving ℝ and ℂ. Since Mathlib wasn't able to synthesise these instances, and the rest of this file fundamentally relies on having them available, I had no choice but to make custom shortcut instances with the backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false flag on them.

It looks like the problem got solved upstream – many thanks to whoever did this! :pray: – and the backward-compatibility flag was removed as part of some subsequent mathlib-wide trawl for no-longer-necessary flags, but it was overlooked that the instances themselves were no longer necessary either.

Anyway, since mathlib can now synthesise both of these instances for itself via general theory, the shortcuts can clearly be removed. Thanks for making the PR!
And thank you for explaining what happened!
